Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G4314 and εἶμι (to go); inaccessible:--which no man can approach.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says God alone has immortality and dwells in light which no man can approach unto, whom no man has seen or can see. The word is inaccessible, light too bright to enter.
TheologicalSignificance: God's light is not dim, it is too bright, and that is why we come to Him through Christ.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
